newsitem.title: FRANCE: MATIF to announce launch of new contracts Friday.
newsitem.headline: MATIF to announce launch of new contracts Friday.

text.p: French futures and options exchange MATIF said on Tuesday it plans to announce the launch of new derivatives contracts on Friday.
MATIF said in a statement it would be holding a news conference on Friday morning. A MATIF spokeswoman declined to give further details.
Market sources said they expected MATIF to launch a French franc five-year bond future and option, and an option on the BOBL contract currently traded on the DTB German futures exchange.

In a series of proposals for new dervative products circulated to MATIF members in February, MATIF said the proposed five-year bond future would have a maturity of four to 5.5 years and a coupon of 4.50 percent.
The proposal said both French franc BTANs and OATs with a residual maturity between four and 5.5 years would be deliverable into the futures contract.
The market sources also said on Tuesday MATIF was planning to carry out a test beginning on April 2 to extend pit-trading hours to 1630 GMT from 1530 GMT currently.
A spokeswoman said MATIF was planning to carry out a test but declined to confirm when it would take place.
MATIF extended the pit-trading session for all its interest rate contracts from this week. Trading now starts at 0730 GMT and ends at 1530 GMT.
MATIF traders said when the initial extension was announced that French labour laws restricting the number of weekly working hours had prevented the session being extended to 1630 GMT immediately.
The head of trading at a large brokerage in Paris said, "It won't really be a test, once it starts the new hours will be set and it will be up to the trading houses to sort it out with their staff."
-- David Clarke, Raoul Sachs, Paris Newsroom +331 4221 5542
